newsitem.title: USA: U.S. unemployment unchanged at 5.2 percent in October.
newsitem.headline: U.S. unemployment unchanged at 5.2 percent in October.

text.p: The unemployment rate was unchanged at 5.2 percent in October, the Labor Department said Friday, as the economy resumed producing new jobs at a healthy pace.
In the government's first look at the the economy's vitality in October, the department said the number of non-farm jobs rose by 210,000 after falling a revised 35,000 in September.
Wall Steet economists surveyed by Reuters had projected an unemployment rate of 5.2 percent and the creation of 212,000 jobs.

The new data comes just two days after the government reported that the economy braked hard in the third quarter, showing a growth rate of only 2.2 percent after speeding ahead at 4.7 percent rate in the second quarter.
Average hourly earnings of workers, which have come under the microscope of late as an indicator of inflation, also were unchanged after being up a revised four cents in September.

The report will be added to the Federal Reserve's deliberations as it meets Nov. 13 to decide the future course of interest rates. Strong job growth will send out some alarms although the lack of wage inflation should be good news.
The department said the services added 119,000 jobs, the largest gain since May, as amusement and recreation added jobs while industry in general showed relatively light layoffs.
Following little growth in August and September, the retail trade added 62,000 in October, with gains fairly widespread.
Government employment continue to show decreases in October, falling an additional 40,000, while employment in both finance and real estate rose sharply.
Manufacturing employment rose 6,000 after falling in September.
